payload.friendly_name: Test doctrine 2: tests-as-scaffold paradigm, tracer bullets and measurement discipline
payload.purpose_context: The first test-doctrine mission shipped the mock-boundary rule. This one finishes that work: the tests-as-scaffold mindset moves out of a binding directive into its own paradigm, the two mocking anti-patterns become named graph nodes, duplicated checklists and long worked examples move into shared reference assets, and the curator profile learns the canonical layout. It also sharpens test-first guidance with vertical tracer-bullet slicing (one behaviour, one failing test, one minimal change), ships a vertical-skeleton-first planning tactic for missions whose work crosses owners, separates refactoring from the red-green loop as a green-mode technique, and adds a measurement discipline so agents sharing a machine do not read killed or contended test runs as results.
payload.purpose_tldr: Give the test doctrine its missing mindset, reference examples and checklists, and teach vertical tracer-bullet slicing and honest test measurement.

payload.question: Which issues and which parts are in this mission?

payload.final_answer: Operator ruling 2026-11-21 (research session, via dispatcher): #216 residue (tests-as-scaffold paradigm with DIRECTIVE_041's mindset split into it, 2 anti-pattern nodes, 4 reference assets, checklist dedup into assets, curator profile update, test-slicing content) closes #216; #154 and #147 in one WP with coordinated tracer-bullet wording, #147 tactic only (directive deferred); #152 in parallel; fold-ins #273 and #274 limited to testing-principles and DIRECTIVE_034.

payload.question: In which order do the parts land?

payload.final_answer: Operator ruling 2026-11-21: #216 paradigm and the 041 split first, then #154/#147; #152 may run in parallel.

Operator ruling 2026-11-21: re-ground against mattpocock/skills HEAD abeeaf9; cite only verified paths (skills/engineering/tdd/SKILL.md, tests.md, mocking.md; skills/engineering/codebase-design/SKILL.md). The old deep-modules.md, interface-design.md and refactoring.md no longer exist.

payload.question: How is the Quad-A asset handled, given the existing quadruple-a-test-format styleguide?

payload.final_answer: Operator answer 2026-11-21: dedup + skeleton + checklist. The quad-a asset holds the language-neutral skeleton and a review checklist; the language styleguides cut their restated definition to a pointer, and their packs add a dependency and a reference edge.

payload.question: Does refactoring stay a step of the TDD loop?

payload.final_answer: Operator answer 2026-11-21: follow upstream (abeeaf9: refactoring is not part of the loop). Refactoring is a green-mode cleanup technique usable inside or outside red-green; extract it as its own interconnected artefacts where feasible (the refactoring catalog and smells).
